messages:
deploy-bot: :rotating_light: Canary report: auth-service v2.3 deployed to canary (10%) - 5xx spike to 6.4% over the last 2m, error pattern: 502 gateway
incident-bot: Paging maya (oncall) -> severity P1, runbook: rollback-or-kill-switch
maya (oncall): I'm on it. Which region? any customer-facing impact?
support-agent: Reports from EU sign-ins failing (timeouts). A few tickets coming in, CS notified customers with workaround.
maya (oncall): ok, thx. @raj can you confirm whether auto-rollback kicked? I don't see an automated rollback in the logs.
raj: auto-rollback didn't trigger. Canary monitor threshold got hit but the autopilot job threw a race on the deployment lock. checking now.
raj: log snippet: `error: deployment lock busy, aborting auto-rollback` — looks like an earlier deploy hold prevented the rollback job from acquiring lock
sophie: Can we flip the feature flag for the new token cache? It's behind ff_auth_token_cache=v2. If we kill that flag we can remove the new path without full service rollback.
alex: Recommend manual rollback of the canary first to stop customer impact quickly, then consider flag flip to mitigate while we root cause the lock.
maya (oncall): agreed. Manual rollback first. @sophie please prepare the rollback command, @alex run verification after.
sophie: Running manual rollback now.


# rollback to stable image
kubectl -n prod set image deploy/auth-service auth-service=redwood/auth-service:v2.2.18
kubectl -n prod rollout status deploy/auth-service --watch

sophie: kubectl accepted, rollout started. pods terminating and replacing.
deploy-bot: Rollout event: auth-service rollout revision -> v2.2.18 initiated by sophie @1769554398
sophie: rollout completed, all canary pods back to v2.2.18
alex: running smoke tests against EU edge
```
GET https://eu-api.redwood.ai/v1/auth/health
expect: 200, latency < 200ms
```
alex: smoke ok, 200s, latency 85ms median, no 5xx in last 1m
support-agent: CS reports logins returning to normal for ticketed customers :thumbsup:
maya (oncall): good. We prevented further impact. Now we need to follow up on why auto-rollback couldn't acquire the lock. @raj can you own the post-incident follow-up and create a tracking issue for the deployment lock race?
raj: will do. Initial hypothesis: two concurrent deploys (hotfix and canary) caused deadlock on our deployment-lock semaphore. I'll attach logs and propose a guarded lock timeout fallback.
sophie: also will open a support ticket to correlate user sessions with failed tokens — root cause may have been token cache invalidation on v2.3.
incident-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-2893 - auth canary caused 5xx spike -> manual rollback performed. Severity P1 -> downgraded to P2 after rollback.
maya (oncall): handing off to @raj for follow-up and postmortem. I'm back on-call but moving to monitoring. If anything re-escalates ping me.
raj: I'll create the postmortem doc and link it here. Action items: (1) fix deployment lock race (owner: eng-deploy) (2) add feature-flag kill-switch automation for token cache (owner: eng-auth) (3) add alpha test for canary image lock contention (owner: eng-runtime)
alex: quick add — verify rollout can be fast-failed if lock not acquired within 10s to allow autopilot to run fallback.
support-agent: CS asks for timeline to include in update: when rollback completed? timestamp?
sophie: rollback completed at 1769554440 (UTC). I'll add that to the incident timeline.
maya (oncall): nice work everyone. I'll close the live incident channel in 30m unless we see regressions. Postmortem ping requested within 48h.
raj: created issue: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-4321 — will include logs and mitigation plan
incident-bot: Routing to #postmortems and #eng-runtime for owners
support-agent: customers notified with status update. no major SLA breaches expected, tracking two minor support tickets.
maya (oncall): closing on-call presence, leaving monitoring to automated alerts. Good cleanup: ensure rollout metrics and canary alerts are annotated in the postmortem.

(reacts: many :thumbsup: and :eyes: in thread)
